$comment: The behaviour suite's CI time budget (#71, FR-013, NFR-001).
The charter's Performance Benchmarks say 'Storybook CI build time under 3 minutes' and
contemplate no test suite at all - ADR-11's own Consequences say 'a new budget has to be
set rather than assumed'. This is that budget, ASSERTED rather than recorded: both jobs
fail above their ceiling, so neither number can go stale silently.
There is deliberately NO `measuredSeconds` field. An earlier revision carried 5.6, which
was contradicted by the very run it cited (6.8s) and by head (11.9s) - a companion number
that nothing re-derives is the prose baseline this whole file argues against. The ceilings
are the record.
TWO ceilings, because they measure different things and mixing them could not tell you
which had regressed. `ceilingSeconds` covers `npm run test` - both lanes, chromium and
webkit in CI. `selftestCeilingSeconds` covers scripts/suite-selftest.mjs, which runs one
full suite per mutation and is where this job's time actually goes. That second key was
read by NOTHING until the second gate pass caught it: an inert key documented as an
enforced ceiling, in the file whose thesis is that stale prose goes unnoticed.
WHERE THIS BUDGET LIVES IS AN OPEN OPERATOR QUESTION. Amending the charter's Performance
Benchmarks may be the right home, but charter.md and charter.yaml contradict each other and
ADR-11's citation for how amendments happen does not check out - see the operator questions
adds the mutations rather than to the end of the mission — the ceiling asserts at the end of
EVERY run and is wired into CI, so it reds at whichever commit pushes the set over, not at a
tidy final measurement pass.

MEASURED AGAIN at #126: 43 mutations / 83 browser tests -> 161.1s CI, 18.9s under the 180s ceiling. That is roughly five more mutations of headroom at the true marginal cost, NOT the "roughly four" this paragraph used to claim from the 41-mutation row.
The harness spawns vitest with `CI: ''`, so it is chromium-only; the second browser affects
`ceilingSeconds` (npm run test), not this one. The two are kept separate so a regression can
be attributed.
DELIBERATE, AND RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT IS A TRADE-OFF: #74 added 18 tests and only 2
standing mutations. Thirteen more survivors were each proven red-first by hand during the
gate fold, but adding them to the standing set would cost ~130s and breach the ceiling. The
next mission to touch this file should raise selftestCeilingSeconds deliberately, with the
run that justifies it, rather than discover the breach.

THE SLOPE, corrected. #74 recorded "~10s per added mutation" and #126 planned around it. That figure bundles two variables: the harness runs one FULL SUITE per mutation, so the two committed CI points (39 mut/62 tests -> 121.7s; 41/80 -> 141.6s) fit per-run ~= 1.90s + 0.0183s x tests. A mutation with no new tests costs ~3.4s; the 10s was a mutation PLUS nine tests. #126 predicted 151s on that fit and CI measured 161.1s, so the model under-predicts by ~7% — good enough to plan with, not good enough to quote.

NOT RAISED at #126, deliberately. Two mutations were added and the run still fits with 18.9s spare, so raising the ceiling would have been raising it from an arithmetic the run does not support — the defect this file records a lens catching twice. The next mission to add mutations should expect to raise it, and now has a real slope to do that from.
